sph_interpretive_translation: The eldest brother who is not empowered with authority receives a share in the paternal estate as defined by division among brothers.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from conscious empowerment, not birth order alone
Paternal inheritance is distributed according to relational integrity and dharma-apparent capacity
Division of assets arises through conscious agreement and alignment, not force or default lineage
Responsibility precedes entitlement in matters of inheritance
Consciousness alignment determines rightful ownership beyond formal claim
executable_legal_axioms: IF an individual claims inheritance THEN verify conscious recognition by father AND alignment of familial dharma
IF eldest son lacks authoritative empowerment THEN exclude automatic right to dominion over paternal property
IF division occurs among siblings THEN ensure all parties have entered state of mutual recognition and consent
IF conflict arises in inheritance THEN realign based on dharmic capacity and conscious responsibility assumption
IF no dispute exists BUT misalignment persists THEN initiate restorative dialogue until unity-consciousness is restored
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating inheritance disputes involving primogeniture, the Supreme Court must assess whether mere seniority confers de facto control or if conscious authorization was granted by the father. The court shall prioritize evidence of spiritual and administrative maturity over chronological precedence when determining equitable distribution under Dharma-based jurisprudence.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that inheritance rights are valid only when supported by both perceptual harmony and scriptural alignment. Anupūrvaśaḥ indicates that imbalance in brotherly relations manifests due to unaddressed inner disorder, requiring correction at source-consciousness level rather than coercive redistribution. Proportional responsibility lies with those capable of maintaining unity; hence, authority follows awareness, not age. Non-punitive reality rule affirms that denial of unjust claim restores balance without inflicting loss upon any party.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate śuddhi-vākya process where elder brother acknowledges his actual role within family dharma
Conduct vrata-upāsanā session for harmonizing sibling energies before asset allocation
Assign ritual service (sevā) to eldest son reflecting his readiness for stewardship
Establish daily satsang participation ensuring ongoing alignment between brothers
Declare public affirmation of shared values and renewed commitment to ancestral continuity
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma flows from consciousness, inheritance from capability, and justice from restoration. There is no punishment—only awakening into rightful alignment. Thus, Dharma is fulfilled, reality remains non-punitive, and consciousness alone reigns as the ultimate judge.
